statement: Let G be a planar graph, v a vertex of degree 5, and c a proper 4-coloring of G-v in which all four colors appear on the neighbors of v; then some single Kempe-chain interchange (swapping two colors on one connected component of the subgraph induced by those two color classes) leaves at most three colors on the neighbors of v, so c extends to a 4-coloring of G.
definitions: Planar graph = finite simple graph drawable in the plane without crossings. Proper coloring = adjacent vertices receive distinct colors. For two colors a,b a Kempe chain is a connected component of the subgraph of G-v induced by the vertices colored a or b; a single Kempe-chain interchange swaps a and b on exactly one such component and changes nothing else. 'Leaves at most three colors on the neighbors of v' refers to the coloring after the interchange; c 'extends' means v can then be given a fourth color.
